payload.lessonGoal: Explain why KV cache dominates long-context serving costs and how CED architecture plus CSA2 compression reduce this footprint.
payload.learnerAssumption: Student understands basic Transformer attention but not specific cache management bottlenecks or DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash optimizations.
payload.centralQuestion: How do architectural changes in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash drastically shrink the KV cache footprint compared to previous models?

requiredClaims.statement: Large KV caches strain HBM and SSD capacity, creating a primary bottleneck for long-context deployment costs.
CSA2 and FP4 caching reduce global KV cache footprint to roughly one-quarter of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
SWA Bounded Replay reduces persistent KV cache footprint to roughly one-eighth of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
CED architecture activates fewer parameters during prefill than decode, improving cost efficiency for input-heavy workloads.

requiredMechanisms.statement: CSA2 shares main KV and indexer K across layers, reducing duplicated cache storage through cross-layer reuse modes.
SWA Bounded Replay reconstructs missing sliding window states by replaying only recent tokens instead of full context.
Causal Encoder-Decoder projects decoder global KV from encoder outputs, halving prefill computation.

scenes.teachingGoal: Demonstrate how CED and CSA2 mechanisms compress KV cache footprints to alleviate HBM and SSD bottlenecks.
scenes.learnerShouldUnderstand: KV cache size drives deployment costs; CED halves prefill compute while CSA2 and SWA replay cut storage needs.
scenes.mentalModel: The model is a factory where memory (KV cache) is expensive inventory; new designs reduce inventory needs without losing output quality.

beats.purpose: Establish the central problem: large KV caches strain hardware capacity and increase costs.
beats.narrationDraft: Long-context agents create massive KV caches that strain HBM and SSD capacity, becoming the primary bottleneck for deployment costs.

beats.purpose: Introduce CED architecture as the first mechanism to reduce prefill computational load.
beats.narrationDraft: The Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture projects decoder global KV from encoder outputs, activating only eight billion parameters during prefill.

beats.purpose: Explain how CSA2 reduces global cache storage through cross-layer sharing.
beats.narrationDraft: Compressed Sparse Attention two shares main KV and indexer keys across layers, cutting global cache storage to roughly one quarter.

beats.purpose: Describe SWA Bounded Replay's role in minimizing persistent cache requirements.
beats.narrationDraft: Sliding Window Attention bounded replay reconstructs local states by reprocessing only recent tokens, avoiding full persistent storage.

beats.purpose: Synthesize the combined impact of all mechanisms on total cache footprint reduction.
beats.narrationDraft: Together these designs reduce global cache to eighty-nine zero bytes per token and persistent cache to one eighth of previous versions.

misconceptions.claim: Reducing KV cache size always degrades model performance significantly.
misconceptions.correction: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash achieves smaller cache footprints while delivering substantially better overall performance than the baseline.

misconceptions.claim: All attention layers must store their own unique KV cache entries.
misconceptions.correction: CSA2 allows layers to share main KV and indexer K across multiple layers, reducing duplicated storage.

evidenceRefs.quote: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2) with FP4 KV caching. These designs reduce its global KV cache footprint (always in HBM) to 890 bytes per token, roughly 1/4 of the corresponding footprint of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Further, through a dedicated deployment optimization known as SWA Bounded Replay, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reduces its persistent KV cache footprint (always on SSD or in host memory) to roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
